# Paul Irving

## Overview

- **Age:** 16  <sub>[v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)</sub>
- **Origin:** Boston, States  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Master Paul  <sub>[v2 c19 P22](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0022)</sub>

## Appearance

Paul has very dark blue eyes and a beautiful, sensitive face of exquisite delicacy and refinement. In his younger years, his face was framed in a halo of chestnut curls, but by age sixteen these gave place to close-cropped brown locks. He is tall for his years and has grown significantly over time.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P1](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0001), [v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v3 c23 P13](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0013), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)_

## Personality

Paul is a sweet, grave, and meditative boy with an imaginative mind that treats fancies and dream-people like real companions. Though deeply poetic and sensitive, he is far from weak, possessing a manly nature, fair-mindedness, and a firm sense of duty. He is polite, cleanly, and well-behaved, yet holds independent thoughts and opinions. As he grows older, his interests broaden to include football alongside his fancies.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c8 P32](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0032), [v2 c8 P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c23 P36](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0036), [v2 c27 P30](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0030), [v2 c27 P62](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0062), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)_

## History

Paul Irving came from Boston to live with his grandmother in Avonlea. Upon starting at the Avonlea school, he quickly formed an intense bond with his teacher, Anne Shirley, who recognized him as a kindred spirit and a child of genius. He entertained himself by creating rich imaginary companions known as his rock people, including Nora and the Twin Sailors. Paul defended his American heritage in a drawn fight against St. Clair Donnell and protected the younger boys at school. He later formed a friendship with Miss Lavendar Lewis, bonding over their shared imaginative minds. When his father, Stephen Irving, unexpectedly arrived in Avonlea, Paul was overjoyed and supported his father's reunion and eventual marriage to Miss Lavendar. Even as he grew older and reached sixteen, his close connection and kindred spirit with Anne remained unchanged.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c11 P42](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0042), [v2 c23 P36](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0036), [v2 c27 P5](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0005), [v2 c27 P51](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0051), [v2 c28 P21](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0021), [v2 c28 P26](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0026), [v2 c28 P45](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0045), [v2 c29 P1](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0001), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)_

## Quotes

> Please, teacher, I found these in Mr. Wright’s field, and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . . I like you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)</sub>

> You see, teacher, it’s just three years today since my little mother died. It’s such a long, long time but it hurts just as much as ever . . . and I miss her just as much as ever. Sometimes it seems to me that I just can’t bear it, it hurts so.  <sub>[v2 c15 P4](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0004)</sub>

> Mrs. Lynde, father made a pretty good job of picking out my first mother and I could trust him to pick out just as good a one the second time.  <sub>[v2 c19 P22](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0022)</sub>

> I’m going to need all my strength of mind to bear up against this, Grandma, and I won’t have any left to grapple with porridge. Oh Grandma, I don’t know what I’ll do when my beautiful teacher goes away.  <sub>[v2 c26 P35](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0035)</sub>

> That’s the beauty of dream-people . . . they stay any age you want them. You and my beautiful teacher and me myself are the only folks in the world that I know of that have dream-people.  <sub>[v2 c27 P62](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0062)</sub>
